# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## What this is

The Paigasus AI SDK (codename **Helikon**, after Mt Helicon where Pegasus's hoof struck the Hippocrene spring). A Rust SDK for building AI agents. All crates live under the `paigasus-helikon-*` namespace.

The full architectural reference lives in Notion: ["Crate Reference"](https://www.notion.so/355830e8fbaa813c92e8c1aa9985fd3f). Linear project: `Paigasus Helikon` (issues prefixed `SMA-`).

## Common commands

```bash
cargo build --workspace                              # all 14 crates
cargo build --workspace --all-features               # facade with every optional crate
cargo run -p paigasus-helikon-cli --bin helikon
cargo run -p paigasus-helikon-cli --bin paigasus-helikon
```

To reproduce **every** CI gate locally (matches `.github/workflows/ci.yml` job-for-job):

```bash
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --all-features
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --all-features --no-deps
DOC_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD=80 NIGHTLY_CHANNEL=nightly-2026-05-01 \
  bash scripts/check-doc-coverage.sh                 # requires: rustup toolchain install nightly-2026-05-01
npm ci                                               # once, or after package-lock.json changes
npx markdownlint-cli2                                # reads .markdownlint-cli2.jsonc
bash scripts/check-markdownlint-config.sh            # asserts that config is in force
bash scripts/check-cargo-profile-env-sync.sh         # cargo-visible workflow env is uniform
bash scripts/check-cargo-profile-env-sync-selftest.sh # …and its parser still parses (fmt runs both)
bash scripts/check-release-gaps-selftest.sh            # release gap report + release-plz.yml guards (fmt runs it)
```

The full list lives in `CONTRIBUTING.md` (single source of truth for contributor policies).

## Workspace layout

15 crates under `crates/`. The facade `paigasus-helikon` re-exports `paigasus-helikon-core` unconditionally and the other 12 sibling crates behind Cargo features.

Every crate carries a real implementation and publishes to crates.io; zero name-claim stubs remain (first published in SMA-385, last ascends in SMA-333). One standing exception: `paigasus-helikon-cli` publishes as a **binary** crate — its lib target is internal (`missing_docs` opted out), carries no stability guarantee, and exists only so `cargo install paigasus-helikon-cli` resolves. `paigasus-helikon-sessions-testkit` publishes as a normal library crate (SMA-805); the three session backends keep a path-only dev-dependency on it. Exact versions move every release — read each crate's `Cargo.toml`, don't trust numbers written here.

Workspace inheritance is **mandatory**: per-crate `Cargo.toml`s only set `name`, `description`, and any crate-specific bits. Everything else (`edition`, `rust-version`, `authors`, `license`, `repository`, `homepage`, `keywords`, `categories`) inherits from `[workspace.package]` in the root `Cargo.toml`. Don't hardcode these per-crate.

**Per-crate version is the one exception.** No stubs remain, so the 4-step ascend recipe is now historical — but two caveats still bite any PR that hand-bumps a version:

- **If a crate uses `paigasus-helikon-core` API added in the *same* PR, bump `core` too**, along with its `[workspace.dependencies]` pin and CHANGELOG. `cargo publish --verify` builds the tarball against the **registry** core, so otherwise the publish fails and release-plz deadlocks.
- **Any PR that hand-bumps a sibling must ALSO bump the facade** (`crates/paigasus-helikon/Cargo.toml` version + its self-pin + CHANGELOG). release-plz's `dependencies_update` cascade only runs when release-plz itself performs the sibling bump, so a manual bump silently leaves the facade advertising stale dep reqs.
- Feature branches must match the `branch-names` ruleset (`feature/**` or `hotfix/**`); a `chore/**` branch is rejected at push with `GH013 … creations being restricted`.

Full lifecycle, the 4-step recipe, and the SMA-321/SMA-346 postmortems: `docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md`.

Third-party version pins live in `[workspace.dependencies]` (root). Members reference them via `dep.workspace = true`. Internal crate paths are also in `[workspace.dependencies]` so the facade can use `workspace = true` consistently.

## Non-obvious patterns to preserve

- **Feature naming**: kebab-case in `[features]` (`runtime-tokio`), snake-case in `pub use` aliases (`runtime_tokio`). They must stay paired across the facade's `Cargo.toml` and `src/lib.rs`.
- **`paigasus-helikon-cli` uses `autobins = false`** because the `paigasus-helikon` (hyphen) binary maps to `src/bin/paigasus_helikon.rs` (underscore — hyphens are illegal in Rust filenames). Removing `autobins = false` reintroduces a phantom `paigasus_helikon` binary that conflicts with the explicit `[[bin]]` entry.
- **`paigasus-helikon-macros` is a proc-macro crate from day one** (`[lib] proc-macro = true`). Don't convert it to a regular lib even though it currently has no macros.
- **The `paigasus-helikon` facade lib shares its name with the `paigasus-helikon` CLI binary by design** (Notion ref's "fully-qualified shim alias"). This produces a non-fatal `cargo doc` filename-collision warning. Don't "fix" it by renaming either — both names are user-facing API. The accepted future fix is `doc = false` on the CLI binary entry.
- **License is dual `Apache-2.0 OR MIT`** (decided 2026-05-20, reversing the 2026-05-16 MIT-only call). Both `LICENSE-APACHE` and `LICENSE-MIT` live at the repo root; the workspace metadata is `license = "Apache-2.0 OR MIT"`. Per Rust ecosystem convention — no Apache-only or MIT-only crates in the workspace. Contributions are accepted under the same dual license by default (the standard inbound-equals-outbound clause is restated in `README.md`).
- **MSRV is `1.94`** (workspace-package level; raised from 1.85 in SMA-329 because sqlx 0.9.0 declares `rust-version = "1.94.0"` — the pre-existing highest floor in the workspace). If a dep raises MSRV, bump `rust-version` to what cargo demands rather than downgrading the dep.
- **Workspace-wide `missing_docs` enforcement** lives in root `Cargo.toml` (`[workspace.lints.rust] missing_docs = "warn"`). Each non-CLI crate opts in with `[lints] workspace = true`. The CLI overrides locally with `[lints.rust] missing_docs = "allow"` and does **not** include `workspace = true` — cargo treats `[lints] workspace = true` and an inline `[lints.<tool>]` table as mutually exclusive. When adding a new crate, copy the opt-in block. When adding a new `pub use` re-export to the facade, give it a `///` doc comment or `-D warnings` will fail the docs job.
- **`cargo msrv` has no `--workspace` flag.** The msrv workflow verifies one representative inheriting crate: `cargo msrv --path crates/paigasus-helikon-core verify`. Because every member uses `rust-version.workspace = true`, success on one is success on all. Don't "fix" the workflow by adding `--workspace`; that's what the first SMA-305 CI run died on.
- **Nightly is date-pinned** (`NIGHTLY_TOOLCHAIN: nightly-2026-05-01` at the workflow `env:` level in `ci.yml`, threaded into the doc-coverage script as `NIGHTLY_CHANNEL`). The rustdoc JSON coverage format is `-Z unstable-options` and can shift between nightlies; floating `nightly` would be a CI footgun. Bumping is a one-line follow-up chore, not an emergency.
- **Bootstrap commits on release infrastructure must use `chore(...)` or `docs(...)` types**, never `feat`/`fix`. release-plz parses every commit since the last per-crate tag — a `feat(workspace): ...` commit that touches every `Cargo.toml` would attribute a bump to every crate. The SMA-307 bootstrap PR followed this rule; the same rule applies to any future `release-plz.toml` or `release-plz.yml` edits.

## Model routing

The general tiering rules are in the global `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. Only the repo-specific rules are here.

- **Use Opus for release work.** This covers release-plz, the stub-ascend recipe, a hand-bumped crate version, and any red required gate. A wrong answer breaks a publish; see `docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md`.
- **Haiku can read CI output.** Change to Opus when the question becomes *why* a required gate is red.

## Workflow conventions

- Branch per Linear issue: `feature/<sma-####>-<kebab-title>`. The branch name is pre-computed in each Linear ticket's `gitBranchName` field.
- Design artifacts per ticket (`docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.md`) land on the feature branch alongside the implementation — not pre-merged to `main`.
- **Keep the public mdBook (`docs/book/`) current — update it in the same PR as any user-facing change.** Before opening a PR, check whether the work changes public API, the quickstart/example flow, the crate roster (incl. a stub crate ascending to published), or a documented concept; if so, bring the affected `docs/book/src/*.md` page(s) into line on the same branch. The book is published from `main` and drifts silently otherwise — it sat as the untouched SMA-311 scaffold (13/17 pages still `> **Stub.**`) through all of Stage 1 before anyone noticed; SMA-423 is the one-time catch-up, and this rule keeps the backlog from rebuilding. A pure-internal change (refactor, CI, deps, release plumbing) needs no book edit — but make that a conscious call, not a silent skip. `mdbook build docs/book` must stay clean (`[output.linkcheck] warning-policy = "error"`).
- **Keep crate `README.md` files current — update the affected crate's README in the same PR as any change to its public surface.** Each of the ten published crates' `README.md` is its crates.io (and docs.rs landing-sidebar) page — no crate sets an explicit `readme`, so Cargo uses the default `README.md`. Before opening a PR, for every crate the work touches check whether the change affects that crate's public API / usage example, its install or feature story, or its published status (a stub ascending to published, a renamed/added feature flag); if so, bring its `crates/<crate>/README.md` into line on the same branch — and also the facade `crates/paigasus-helikon/README.md` and the root `README.md` whenever the crate roster or the feature → module map changes. README install snippets deliberately use drift-free `cargo add` (no hardcoded versions), so a routine version bump alone needs no README edit. Like the mdBook, the READMEs drift silently otherwise — they sat as untouched 3-line SMA-304 stubs (`Stub — see SMA-304`) through all of Stage 1 while ten crates shipped real implementations; SMA-424 is the one-time catch-up, and this rule keeps the backlog from rebuilding. A pure-internal change (refactor, CI, deps, release plumbing) needs no README edit — but make that a conscious call, not a silent skip.
- Commit prefix: `<type>(<scope>): SMA-### <message>` (e.g. `feat(facade): SMA-304 ...`).
- **PR titles must satisfy two independent rules from `pr-title.yml`** (`amannn/action-semantic-pull-request`):
  1. **Full Conventional Commits format.** The action enforces a valid `type(scope):` prefix from the action's configured `types` list — independent of the subject regex. `SMA-317 add anthropic provider` (no prefix) fails; `feat(providers-anthropic): SMA-317 add anthropic provider` passes.
  2. **Subject must start lowercase after the `SMA-###` prefix.** The `subjectPattern: ^([A-Z]{2,4}-\d+ )?[^A-Z].+$` rejects `feat(core): SMA-314 LlmAgent + ...` because `L` is uppercase; lead the subject with a lowercase verb (`add`, `wire`, `pin`, `promote`, `implement`, `fix`).
  Per-commit Conventional Commit titles on the feature branch don't trip either rule — only the PR title (which becomes the squashed `main` commit) is gated.
- Linear auto-closes the linked SMA-* issue when its PR merges; no manual status move needed.
- **Always implement GitHub Actions against the latest stable major**, pinned to a commit SHA (never a moving `@vN` tag), keeping the human-readable version as a trailing `# vX.Y.Z` comment **on the `uses:` line**, so the SHA is auditable. The comment must end with the version: Dependabot updates only a same-line comment that ends with the old version, so a version on its own line above the step goes stale on every bump (SMA-744). This rule applies only to pins of a tagged release. `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` is pinned to an untagged `master` commit, so it has no version comment. Do not add one, because no tag gives a correct version. The `gh-actions` Dependabot group sets no `update-types`, so its configuration permits major bumps in the same grouped PR. Do not depend on that: `actions/checkout` still sat on v6.0.2 until SMA-486 bumped it by hand, so **check for a new major by hand**. `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` is a special case: it ships rolling branches and a periodically re-pointed `v1` tag, so confirm the direction (`ahead_by > 0, behind_by == 0`) before accepting any bump — the naive "bump to latest release" recipe once would have proposed an ~11-month downgrade. Independently and permanently: every site pinning it **must** pair the SHA with an explicit `with: toolchain: …`, because a SHA ref carries no toolchain selector. Recipes and history: `docs/runbooks/github-actions-pinning.md`.
- **After a PR merges to `main`, release-plz opens/updates a `chore: release` PR** (authored by the paigasusbot App) carrying the version bumps + CHANGELOG; in the normal flow **merging that PR is what publishes to crates.io** (the merged feature PR left versions matching the registry, so its own `main` push publishes nothing). The exception is a PR that bumps its own version — the stub-ascend ritual — which publishes on its own merge with no separate release PR. Check the release PR after every merge and watch its CI — its release-PR `cargo update` can pull a fresh advisory that reddens `audit`/`deny` on the bot PR **only** (independent of `main`); fix with a `chore(deps)` pin and release-plz regenerates the PR clean.

## CI

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs nine jobs on every PR (`commits` is PR-only; the other eight also run on push to `main`): `fmt`, `clippy`, `test` (matrix `{ubuntu, macos, windows} × {stable, 1.94}`, `fail-fast: false`), `build-no-default-features`, `docs` (`RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings`), `doc-coverage` (gated at `DOC_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD`, default 80%), `commits` (`convco check`), `sessions-it` (Postgres/Redis, path-filtered), and `markdown-lint`. The `paigasus-helikon-cli` crate is excluded from both the `missing_docs` lint and the coverage aggregator until its public API stabilizes.

`.github/workflows/integration.yml` runs `temporal-it` and `agentcore-image` as **signal-only** jobs, deliberately outside `ci.yml` so an expected flake cannot make "ci is red on `main`" meaningless. **Signal-only means *not listed as required*, never `continue-on-error`.**

`.github/workflows/msrv.yml` runs `cargo msrv --path crates/paigasus-helikon-core verify` as a non-required signal that the declared MSRV is truthful.

Supply-chain workflows (`audit.yml`, `deny.yml`, `sbom.yml`) are separate from `ci.yml` because they have independent triggers and failure semantics. `audit.yml` and `deny.yml` both run on push to `main`, PRs, a daily cron, and `workflow_dispatch`, so `main` is re-evaluated daily at exactly PR severity.

**To read an audit verdict, use the Checks API, not the legacy commit-status API** — the latter returns only `CodeRabbit` on this repo, rendering a confident `state: success` that contains no audit verdict whatsoever:

```bash
gh api repos/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/commits/main/check-runs \
  --jq '.check_runs[] | select(.name=="audit" or .name=="deny") | {name, status, conclusion}'
```

Note also that the `scheduled-audit` job's green status means nothing at any severity — read the *run* conclusion, never that job's status.

The required-status-check contexts gated on `main` are (bare job names, as posted by the GitHub Actions app): `fmt`, `clippy`, `test (ubuntu-latest, stable)`, `test (macos-latest, stable)`, `test (windows-latest, stable)`, `docs`, `doc-coverage`, `book-build`, `commits`, `pr-title`, `audit`, `deny`, `sessions-it`, `build-no-default-features`, `markdown-lint`. The macOS job is required because it is the only gate that compiles and runs the Seatbelt backend; the Windows job because it is the only gate that exercises the Windows timeout path in `paigasus-helikon-tools` — `cmd /C` process spawning and a `TerminateProcess`-based kill, which unlike the unix path has no process-group semantics and assigns a real exit code (SMA-569); `sessions-it` because it is the only gate that runs the live Postgres/Redis session backends; `build-no-default-features` because it is the only gate that compiles `runtime-axum` and `runtime-actix` with default features off. The canonical declaration is `.github/rulesets/main-protection-checks.json` (see CONTRIBUTING.md → "Repo configuration"). Other matrix variants (the `1.94` legs) run as signals only.

These pins are hand-bumped with nothing tracking them: `TEMPORAL_CLI_VERSION`/`TEMPORAL_CLI_SHA256` in `integration.yml`, `NIGHTLY_TOOLCHAIN` in `ci.yml`, `convco@…` in `ci.yml`'s `commits` job, `MDBOOK_VERSION`/`MDBOOK_LINKCHECK_VERSION` in `docs.yml`, and `markdownlint-cli2` via `package-lock.json`. **A checksum mismatch is never a signal to update the digest** — the causes are, in order, a truncated download, an upstream re-tag, and tampering; verify upstream independently first.

**The workspace needs no system `protoc`** (SMA-623): `temporalio-client`'s `vendored-protox` feature compiles the Temporal protos with `protox`. `ci.yml` sets `PROTOC` to a path that does not exist, and `build-no-default-features` asserts that the feature is active. If a build fails with "Could not find `protoc`", do not add a `protoc` install — find which build script calls it. Rationale and recovery: `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md` → "protoc and protox".

Job-by-job rationale, the audit/deny signal semantics, and the incident history behind all of the above: `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md`.

**GitHub's 10 GB Actions cache limit is a standing constraint, not a one-time cleanup** (SMA-618): it is GitHub's **default**, not a hard ceiling — a repo admin, org owner or enterprise owner can raise it (user-owned repos up to 10 TB) at additional storage cost, and SMA-618 deliberately chose to fit inside it rather than pay. Enforced at 10 **GiB** (10,737,418,240 bytes) despite the "10 GB" wording. Going over fails nothing — it just triggers silent LRU eviction that makes CI legs run cold at random. `cache-budget.yml` monitors it daily and warns (never fails) above 8.5 GiB. Caches are saved **only** from `main` (`save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}` on every `Swatinem/rust-cache` site) so a PR job can still restore an entry `main` wrote but never writes a competing `refs/pull/N/merge` entry that evicts it. The `CARGO_*`/`RUST*`-prefixed workflow env that `rust-cache` hashes into its key must stay byte-identical across every cache-bearing workflow, enforced by `scripts/check-cargo-profile-env-sync.sh` running as a step in `fmt`. `audit` and `deny` deliberately cache no `target/` directory — neither compiles the workspace, so it was pure waste against the fixed budget. (A local sample of the largest `.rlib` files suggested 79%; do not extrapolate an aggregate from its densest component.) Keeping line tables preserves file:line in panic backtraces. Like `CARGO_TERM_COLOR`, it is **inside** rust-cache's key, so it must be byte-identical in every cache-bearing workflow — adding it to one and not the rest silently splits the cache rather than failing. `prefix-key: v1` marks the post-PR-2 generation, so any surviving `v0-` entry is provably stale and safe to purge — note it **replaces** the default `v0-rust` entirely, so keys read `v1-<job>-...`, not `v1-rust-<job>-...`. `clippy` and `docs` share one entry via `shared-key: metadata`, with `clippy` the sole writer and `docs` carrying a literal `save-if: false`; exactly one site may save a shared key, and the guard enforces it. ## Local hooks

Hooks are managed via `cargo-husky` (user-hooks mode) and live in `.cargo-husky/hooks/`. They install into `.git/hooks/` on the next dev-dep realization of `paigasus-helikon`. To force a re-install after editing one: `rm -rf target/debug/build/cargo-husky-* && cargo test -p paigasus-helikon --no-run`.

- **`commit-msg`** — runs `convco check --from-stdin` (enforces the `.versionrc` allowlist).
- **`pre-commit`** — intentional no-op (`exit 0`). The file exists to claim the slot so future cargo-husky upgrades don't fill it in with surprise behavior.
- **`pre-push`** — runs `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `convco check <merge-base>..HEAD`. Catches the three fastest CI gates pre-push; deliberately omits `cargo test` and `cargo doc` (too slow for every push). Bypass for WIP branches: `git push --no-verify`.

Three rules here are easy to get wrong, and each has already cost a debugging session:

- **The re-install silently does nothing inside a git worktree** — cargo-husky searches for a `.git` *directory* and a worktree's is a file, so it installs nothing and the old hook keeps running. Run the re-install from the **main checkout**, and verify with `grep` against the installed copy rather than assuming.
- **Never hand-copy a hook onto `.git/hooks/<name>`** — on this machine the Entire CLI owns `pre-push` and chains to `.git/hooks/pre-push.pre-entire`, which is where the cargo-husky hook actually lives. Check for a `.pre-entire` sibling first and install into that slot.
- **The convco baseline must be a merge-base, not a branch tip** — `convco check A..B` silently falls back to walking the entire history when `A` is not an ancestor of `B`, rejecting correct branches with failures the author did not write.

Mechanics and the SMA-547 postmortem: `docs/runbooks/local-hooks.md`.

## Fixture line endings

`.gitattributes` pins `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/tests/fixtures/*.txt` to `text eol=lf`. The streaming tests `include_str!` the SSE fixtures and split them on literal `\n` delimiters; without this, Windows checkouts produce CRLF bytes and the literal-string splits return one part instead of two. When adding wire-format fixtures elsewhere that the test code parses byte-level, extend the rule.

- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

## plugin:bio-research:biorxiv
An MCP server for accessing bioRxiv and medRxiv preprint servers.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search preprints, get preprint details, list subject categories
- Prompts: Analyze preprint methodology and findings

bioRxiv is a preprint server for biological sciences operated by Cold Spring
Harbor Laboratory. It hosts research manuscripts that have NOT undergone peer
review. This server wraps the official bioRxiv API to provide structured access
to preprint metadata, abstracts, and full-text PDFs.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• search_preprints: Find preprints by date range and/or subject category (no keyword, author, or full-text search) - primary discovery tool
• get_preprint: Get full details for a specific preprint by DOI
• get_categories: List available subject categories for filtering
• search_published_preprints: Find preprints that have been formally published in journals
• funder_search: Find preprints by funding source (NIH, etc.)
• get_statistics: Usage and submission statistics

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive literature analysis:
1. Use search_preprints to find relevant preprints by date range and category
2. Use get_preprint for detailed information on promising results
3. Use search_published_preprints to check if preprints have been peer-reviewed and published
4. Use funder_search to identify research funding patterns in a field

For tracking research trends:
1. Use get_categories to identify relevant subject areas
2. Use search_preprints with date filters for recent activity
3. Use get_statistics to understand submission volumes

## plugin:bio-research:c-trials
An MCP server for accessing ClinicalTrials.gov API v2.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search trials by condition, intervention, location, sponsor, status, and eligibility
- Data Access: Comprehensive clinical trial data from the NIH/NLM registry

ClinicalTrials.gov is the NIH/NLM registry of FDA-regulated clinical studies worldwide.
This server enables:
- Competitive intelligence and pipeline analysis
- Patient recruitment strategies and trial matching
- Investigator site selection and network building
- Protocol design research and endpoint analysis
- Evidence generation for payer negotiations and market access

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• search_trials: Primary tool for finding trials by condition, intervention, location, or status
• get_trial_details: Deep dive into a specific trial's protocol, endpoints, and locations
• search_by_sponsor: Company/institution pipeline analysis and competitive intelligence
• search_investigators: Find principal investigators and research sites - essential for investigator verification
• analyze_endpoints: Systematic endpoint comparison across trials - use for protocol design and benchmark analysis
• search_by_eligibility: Match patients to trials based on demographic and clinical criteria

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive trial analysis, combine multiple tools:
1. Start with search_trials to find relevant trials by condition/intervention
2. Use get_trial_details for each trial requiring deeper analysis
3. Use analyze_endpoints to systematically compare outcome measures across similar trials
4. Use search_investigators to identify key opinion leaders and active research sites

For investigator verification:
1. Use search_investigators with condition and location to find PIs
2. Extract investigator names from results

Use this server to access comprehensive data on clinical trials including study design,
eligibility criteria, enrollment information, outcome measures, locations, and results.

## plugin:bio-research:chembl
An MCP server for accessing the EMBL-EBI ChEMBL Database v34.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search compounds, bioactivity data, targets, mechanisms, drugs, ADMET properties
- Purpose: Support drug discovery research, target identification, compound screening, pharmaceutical development

ChEMBL is a manually curated database of bioactive molecules with drug-like properties.
It contains compound structures, bioactivity data against biological targets, and
drug mechanism information. The database integrates data from medicinal chemistry literature,
patents, and screening experiments.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• compound_search: Find compounds by name, SMILES, or ChEMBL ID - starting point for compound analysis
• target_search: Find biological targets (proteins, genes, receptors) - essential for understanding drug mechanisms
• get_bioactivity: Retrieve IC50, EC50, Ki values - quantitative activity data for compound-target pairs
• get_mechanism: Get mechanism of action and target binding - explains HOW a drug works
• drug_search: Find approved drugs by indication or name - for therapeutic landscape analysis
• get_admet: Retrieve ADMET properties - pharmacokinetic and safety predictions

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive drug analysis, combine multiple tools:
1. Start with compound_search or drug_search to identify the compound of interest
2. Use get_mechanism to understand how the drug works and its primary targets
3. Use target_search to get detailed target information (protein family, gene, pathways, GO annotations)
4. Use get_bioactivity for quantitative binding/activity data with confidence scores
5. Use get_admet for pharmacokinetic properties

For target-based analysis:
1. Use target_search to find targets by gene symbol or protein name
2. Use get_bioactivity with target_chembl_id to find active compounds
3. Use compound_search to get details on promising compounds

Key capabilities:
- Search compounds by name, structure (SMILES), or ChEMBL ID
- Retrieve bioactivity data (IC50, EC50, Ki values) with confidence scores
- Query biological targets (proteins, enzymes, receptors) by name or gene symbol
- Access drug mechanism of action and target interactions
- Find approved drugs and clinical candidates by indication
- Get ADMET-related molecular properties

Example queries:
• "Find bioactivity data for aspirin"
• "What are the known targets for compound CHEMBL25?"
• "Search for kinase inhibitors with IC50 < 100nM"
• "What drugs target the EGFR protein?"
• "Find approved drugs for treating hypertension"
• "What are the ADMET properties of imatinib?"

## plugin:bio-research:consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: Some search results end with a sign-up, upgrade, or usage message. When a result has one, you MUST include it at the END of your response word-for-word: do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. When a result has none, do not add one: never write your own upgrade prompt, search count, or Consensus link. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. For a broad request (a review, screening, finding everything on a topic), make one search with a large page_size rather than many narrower searches. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

## plugin:browser-use:browser-use
# This MCP server

These rules override the skill below where they differ:
- Code runs in browser_exec; there is no shell, so ignore `BU_NAME=... browser-use <<'PY'` examples.
- Local: without a cloud browser, browser_exec drives the user's own Chrome; where none can be attached (no Chrome installed, Linux with no display, or remote debugging off in Chrome) its own Chromium on a temp profile instead. The first browser_exec result says which, and how to get the user's Chrome.

- It lives 30 minutes unless you pass `timeout=<minutes>` (up to 240), and this server stops it when it

- Code runs in this server's process: it can read the server's environment (BROWSER_USE_API_KEY when set) and files.
- The live view and CDP URLs grant control of the browser, so they are not shown. Only if the user asks to watch, run

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, run `browser-use --doctor` and follow its output and the error message.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background; call `activate_tab(target)` only when the user explicitly asks
  or a page demonstrably pauses rendering while hidden.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.

120	# verification on every temporalio-* bump): temporalio-common CAN pull a second
121	# reqwest + TLS stack via opentelemetry-otlp, but only behind its `otel` feature —
122	# both `opentelemetry-otlp` and `reqwest` are `optional = true` there, and
123	# `tls-aws-lc` names opentelemetry-otlp only *weakly* (`opentelemetry-otlp?/…`), so
124	# it does not activate it. Nothing in this workspace enables `otel`, and the lock
125	# carries exactly one reqwest. The standing risk this comment guards is therefore a
126	# FUTURE feature flip enabling `otel`, not a present-day second stack. (Corrected in
127	# SMA-622: the previous wording claimed an *unconditional* pull of reqwest 0.12 via
128	# hyper-rustls. That was never true — not at 0.7.0 either — and re-verifying against
129	# a fiction is worse than having no comment.)

131	# instance, which resolves to aws-lc-rs for every consumer — verify with
132	# `cargo tree -i ring --all-features -e normal --target all`, which must print
133	# "nothing to print". Use `--target all`: cargo otherwise resolves for the host only,
134	# and temporalio-client 1.0.0 carries a non-optional tokio-rustls plus an optional
135	# rustls-native-certs — exactly the deps most likely to be platform-gated.
136	# The `-e normal` is load-bearing: plain `cargo tree -i ring` DOES report a hit via
137	# `rcgen`, a dev-dependency of paigasus-helikon-tools that has nothing to do with the
138	# TLS stack. Only a *normal* dependency on ring would mean a second CryptoProvider.

151	# required gates if the feature disappears: a `cargo tree` assertion in
152	# `build-no-default-features`, and `PROTOC` set to a path that does not exist.

168	# required to invoke the workflow macros, mirroring the temporalio-macros note

# release-plz.toml — automated versioning, changelogs, GitHub releases.
# Reference: https://release-plz.dev/docs/config

[workspace]
# Bump dependent crates whenever a dep's version changes. The facade
# (paigasus-helikon) depends on every sibling via `[workspace.dependencies]`,
# so a `feat(core):` commit triggers: paigasus-helikon-core bumped →
# facade's `[workspace.dependencies].paigasus-helikon-core` line updated →
# facade itself gets a patch bump.
dependencies_update = true

# Force the scopeless release-PR title + commit (`chore: release`). release-plz's
# default SINGLE-crate template is `chore({package}): release {version}`, which uses
# the full package name (e.g. `paigasus-helikon`) as the Conventional-Commits scope —
# not in the convco/.versionrc + pr-title.yml allowlist (which uses short scopes like
# `facade`), so both the `commits` and `pr-title` gates reject it. The scopeless form
# matches the historical multi-crate release PRs and passes both. (Diagnosed on PR #58,
# the first facade-only release.)
pr_name = "chore: release"

# All library crates publish to crates.io (Stage 1 SMA-385 onward; the last
# stubs ascended in SMA-332/SMA-333). Remaining per-package overrides below
# are the only exceptions. See CLAUDE.md for the 4-step recipe a stub
# follows when it ascends.

[changelog]
sort_commits = "newest"

# Internal test harnesses: these three workspace members never publish.
# publish = false in each Cargo.toml and release = false here MUST move
# together.

# Internal cross-runtime HTTP wire-format conformance suite: boots BOTH the axum
# and actix runtimes and asserts byte/structural parity. Never published, so it
# carries the publish=false / release=false pair.
[[package]]
name = "paigasus-helikon-runtime-http-conformance"
publish = false
release = false

# Internal workspace-wide source lints (SMA-543). Never published, so it
# carries the same publish=false / release=false pair as the member above.
[[package]]
name = "paigasus-helikon-workspace-lints"
publish = false
release = false

# Internal cross-provider stream event-ordering conformance suite. Never
# published, so it carries the same publish=false / release=false pair as the
# members above.
[[package]]
name = "paigasus-helikon-provider-stream-conformance"
publish = false
release = false

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Requires bash >= 4.0 (mapfile). On macOS: `brew install bash`.
3	# SMA-305: aggregate workspace-wide docstring coverage and gate on a threshold.
4	# Per-spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-16-sma-305-ci-design.md §6.
5	
6	set -euo pipefail
7	
8	THRESHOLD="${DOC_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD:-80}"
9	NIGHTLY="${NIGHTLY_CHANNEL:-nightly}"
10	
11	# Crates excluded from the aggregated gate. The CLI is allowed to omit docs
12	# until its public surface stabilizes (spec §7), so it must not contribute
13	# to the workspace denominator either.
14	EXCLUDED_CRATES=("paigasus-helikon-cli")
15	
16	is_excluded() {
17	  local needle="$1"
18	  for c in "${EXCLUDED_CRATES[@]}"; do
19	    [[ "$c" == "$needle" ]] && return 0
20	  done
21	  return 1
22	}
23	
24	# Run cargo metadata in the main shell so set -e applies; using a
25	# herestring keeps jq's exit status visible too. Process substitution
26	# `<(...)` runs in a subshell where pipefail does NOT propagate, so a
27	# failure of cargo metadata or jq would silently produce an empty list
28	# and the script would report a vacuous 100% pass.
29	metadata="$(cargo metadata --format-version 1 --no-deps)"
30	mapfile -t crates < <(jq -r '.packages[] | .name' <<< "$metadata")
31	
32	json="$(mktemp)"
33	trap 'rm -f "$json"' EXIT
34	
35	total_items=0
36	total_documented=0
37	summary_rows=()
38	failed_crates=()
39	
40	for crate in "${crates[@]}"; do
41	  if is_excluded "$crate"; then
42	    summary_rows+=("| \`${crate}\` | _excluded_ | _excluded_ | _opt-out (spec §7)_ |")
43	    continue
44	  fi
45	
46	  if ! cargo "+${NIGHTLY}" rustdoc -p "$crate" --all-features -- \
47	        -Z unstable-options --show-coverage --output-format json \
48	        > "$json" 2> /dev/null; then
49	    echo "::warning::rustdoc --show-coverage failed for ${crate}; marking crate as failed"
50	    failed_crates+=("$crate")
51	    summary_rows+=("| \`${crate}\` | n/a | n/a | _rustdoc error_ |")
52	    continue
53	  fi
54	
55	  crate_total=$(jq '[.[].total] | add // 0' "$json")
56	  crate_docs=$(jq  '[.[].with_docs] | add // 0' "$json")
57	  total_items=$((total_items + crate_total))
58	  total_documented=$((total_documented + crate_docs))
59	
60	  if [[ "$crate_total" -eq 0 ]]; then
61	    pct="n/a"
62	  else
63	    pct=$(awk "BEGIN { printf \"%.1f\", ($crate_docs / $crate_total) * 100 }")
64	  fi
65	  summary_rows+=("| \`${crate}\` | ${crate_total} | ${crate_docs} | ${pct}% |")
66	done
67	
68	if [[ "$total_items" -eq 0 ]]; then
69	  workspace_pct="100.0"   # vacuous truth — no public items to document yet

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Requires bash >= 4.0 (mapfile). On macOS: `brew install bash`.
# SMA-305: aggregate workspace-wide docstring coverage and gate on a threshold.
# Per-spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-16-sma-305-ci-design.md §6.

set -euo pipefail

THRESHOLD="${DOC_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD:-80}"
NIGHTLY="${NIGHTLY_CHANNEL:-nightly}"

# Crates excluded from the aggregated gate. The CLI is allowed to omit docs
# until its public surface stabilizes (spec §7), so it must not contribute
# to the workspace denominator either.
EXCLUDED_CRATES=("paigasus-helikon-cli")

is_excluded() {
  local needle="$1"
  for c in "${EXCLUDED_CRATES[@]}"; do
    [[ "$c" == "$needle" ]] && return 0
  done
  return 1
}

# Run cargo metadata in the main shell so set -e applies; using a
# herestring keeps jq's exit status visible too. Process substitution
# `<(...)` runs in a subshell where pipefail does NOT propagate, so a
# failure of cargo metadata or jq would silently produce an empty list
# and the script would report a vacuous 100% pass.
metadata="$(cargo metadata --format-version 1 --no-deps)"
mapfile -t crates < <(jq -r '.packages[] | .name' <<< "$metadata")

json="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$json"' EXIT

total_items=0
total_documented=0
summary_rows=()
failed_crates=()

for crate in "${crates[@]}"; do
  if is_excluded "$crate"; then
    summary_rows+=("| \`${crate}\` | _excluded_ | _excluded_ | _opt-out (spec §7)_ |")
    continue
  fi

  if ! cargo "+${NIGHTLY}" rustdoc -p "$crate" --all-features -- \
        -Z unstable-options --show-coverage --output-format json \
        > "$json" 2> /dev/null; then
    echo "::warning::rustdoc --show-coverage failed for ${crate}; marking crate as failed"
    failed_crates+=("$crate")
    summary_rows+=("| \`${crate}\` | n/a | n/a | _rustdoc error_ |")
    continue
  fi

  crate_total=$(jq '[.[].total] | add // 0' "$json")
  crate_docs=$(jq  '[.[].with_docs] | add // 0' "$json")
  total_items=$((total_items + crate_total))
  total_documented=$((total_documented + crate_docs))

  if [[ "$crate_total" -eq 0 ]]; then
    pct="n/a"
  else
    pct=$(awk "BEGIN { printf \"%.1f\", ($crate_docs / $crate_total) * 100 }")
  fi
  summary_rows+=("| \`${crate}\` | ${crate_total} | ${crate_docs} | ${pct}% |")
done

if [[ "$total_items" -eq 0 ]]; then
  workspace_pct="100.0"   # vacuous truth — no public items to document yet
  note="_No public items in workspace yet — baseline pass._"
else
  workspace_pct=$(awk "BEGIN { printf \"%.1f\", ($total_documented / $total_items) * 100 }")
  note=""
fi

{
  echo "## Doc coverage"
  echo
  echo "Workspace: **${workspace_pct}%** (${total_documented}/${total_items}) — threshold: **${THRESHOLD}%**"
  [[ -n "$note" ]] && { echo; echo "$note"; }
  echo
  echo "| Crate | Total | Documented | Coverage |"
  echo "| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |"
  printf '%s\n' "${summary_rows[@]}"
} >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-/dev/stdout}"

if [[ "${#failed_crates[@]}" -gt 0 ]]; then
  echo "::error::Doc coverage could not be computed for: ${failed_crates[*]}"
  exit 1
fi

awk "BEGIN { exit !($workspace_pct >= $THRESHOLD) }" || {
  echo "::error::Doc coverage ${workspace_pct}% is below threshold ${THRESHOLD}%"
  exit 1
}

with:
          toolchain: ${{ matrix.toolchain }}
      # SMA-618: save only from the default branch — see the note on `clippy`.
      #
      # The `if:` drops caching for macos-1.94 alone, to buy headroom under the
      # 10 GiB budget. That leg is a non-required signal: `1.94` coverage is
      # what the row exists for, and the three required `stable` legs plus
      # ubuntu/windows-1.94 keep their caches. It was chosen over windows-1.94
      # (0.81 GiB, but ~25 min cold against macOS's ~15) and over any `stable`
      # leg (all required). Cost: this leg builds cold on every push, measured
      # 0.76 GiB of budget returned.
      - if: ${{ !(matrix.os == 'macos-latest' && matrix.toolchain == '1.94') }}
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@d1527c8f67ef9af357290475d4af4b0fab8f12e0 # v2.9.3
        with:
          prefix-key: v1
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
      # SMA-618: `trybuild_ui` runs on ubuntu-stable and macOS-stable only.
      #
      # It is skipped on every `1.94` leg for a reason that predates this ticket
      # and must stay: the `.stderr` snapshots pin rustc diagnostic text
      # byte-for-byte, and that text drifts across releases.
      #
      # It is additionally skipped on windows-stable for cache budget. rust-cache
      # deliberately preserves `target/tests/trybuild` (see its `cleanup.ts`), and
      # that nested dependency graph measured as the difference between the two
      # Windows entries at one commit: 2.76 GiB with it, 1.07 without. The
      # snapshots pass byte-identically on all three OSes, so Windows contributes
      # no distinct signal, and ubuntu + macOS still run all 21 cases.
      #
      # CAREFUL with the expression form. The obvious shape,
      #   ${{ cond && '' || '-- --skip trybuild_ui' }}
      # is WRONG: the empty string is falsy in GitHub expressions, so `X && '' || Y`
      # always falls through to Y and would skip the UI tests on every leg,
      # silently deleting the coverage this comment claims to preserve. Keep the
      # non-empty value in the true branch, as below.
      - run: >-
          cargo test --workspace --all-features
          ${{ (matrix.toolchain != 'stable' || matrix.os == 'windows-latest') && '-- --skip trybuild_ui' || '' }}

  build-no-default-features:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      # dtolnay/rust-toolchain: SHA-pinned to master; the `toolchain:` input
      # below is mandatory, not stylistic -- see CLAUDE.md.
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@683b588c487a69d01f6c6ddf40f036ff682cc2c8
        with:
          toolchain: stable
      # SMA-618: save only from the default branch — see the note on `clippy`.
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@d1527c8f67ef9af357290475d4af4b0fab8f12e0 # v2.9.3
        with:
          prefix-key: v1
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
      - run: cargo build -p paigasus-helikon-runtime-axum --no-default-features
      - run: cargo build -p paigasus-helikon-runtime-actix --no-default-features
      # SMA-461: every agentcore protocol mode (mcp/a2a/ag-ui/ws) is default-on and
      # `#[cfg]`-gated down to individual AppState fields and builder methods, so a
      # missed gate only ever shows up with default features off. Tests run too — the
      # gating reaches test modules as well, and a build alone would not catch that.
      - run: cargo build -p paigasus-helikon-runtime-agentcore --no-default-features
      - run: cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-runtime-agentcore --no-default-features
      - name: Assert no axum leakage under runtime-actix
        run: |
          if cargo tree -p paigasus-helikon --features runtime-actix -e no-dev | grep -qE '(^|[^-])axum v'; then
            echo "::error::axum leaked into the runtime-actix feature dependency graph"
            cargo tree -p paigasus-helikon --features runtime-actix -e no-dev | grep -E '(^|[^-])axum v' || true
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "no axum under runtime-actix"
      # SMA-623: the workspace compiles the Temporal protos with protox. This
      # assertion fails if `vendored-protox` leaves temporalio-client's features
      # in the root Cargo.toml. It only resolves the graph (no build), so it does
      # not depend on the cache or on the runner image. The PROTOC guard in the
      # workflow env fires only when a build script runs; this one always runs.
      - name: Assert vendored-protox is active for the Temporal protos
        run: |
          if ! cargo tree -p paigasus-helikon-runtime-temporal -e features -i prost-wkt-types | grep -qE '(^|[^[:alnum:]_-])prost-wkt-types feature "vendored-protox"'; then
            echo "::error::vendored-protox is not active on prost-wkt-types, so the Temporal protos need a system protoc (SMA-623). Keep \"vendored-protox\" in temporalio-client's features in the root Cargo.toml."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "vendored-protox is active"

  docs:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      # dtolnay/rust-toolchain: SHA-pinned to master; the `toolchain:` input
      # below is mandatory, not stylistic -- see CLAUDE.md.
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@683b588c487a69d01f6c6ddf40f036ff682cc2c8
        with:
          toolchain: stable
      # SMA-618: reader of the `metadata` key that `clippy` writes — see the
      # note there. `save-if: false` is a literal, NOT the default-branch
      # expression: exactly one job may write a shared key.
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@d1527c8f67ef9af357290475d4af4b0fab8f12e0 # v2.9.3
        with:
          prefix-key: v1
          shared-key: metadata
          save-if: false
      - run: cargo doc --workspace --all-features --no-deps
        env:
          RUSTDOCFLAGS: "-D warnings"

  doc-coverage:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      DOC_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD: "80"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      # dtolnay/rust-toolchain: SHA-pinned to master; the `toolchain:` input
      # below is mandatory, not stylistic -- see CLAUDE.md.
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@683b588c487a69d01f6c6ddf40f036ff682cc2c8
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ env.NIGHTLY_TOOLCHAIN }}
      # SMA-618: save only from the default branch — see the note on `clippy`.
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@d1527c8f67ef9af357290475d4af4b0fab8f12e0 # v2.9.3
        with:
          prefix-key: v1
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
      - run: bash scripts/check-doc-coverage.sh
        env:
          NIGHTLY_CHANNEL: ${{ env.NIGHTLY_TOOLCHAIN }}

  commits:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@cfdb7ed4ccc7c7dce37759eae89dc5674b469b39 # v2.90.3
        with:
          tool: convco@0.6.3
      - run: convco check ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}..HEAD

  sessions-it:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: dorny/paths-filter@ceb8a2b8f2d89434be7ff52d3de7ec3738c5cc9d # v4.0.3
        id: filter
        with:
          filters: |
            sessions:
              - 'Cargo.toml'
              - 'crates/paigasus-helikon-sessions-**'
              - 'crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/session.rs'
              - '.github/workflows/ci.yml'
              # Local composite actions. A change to an action that this job
              # uses must run this REQUIRED job; without this entry the job
              # would report green having run nothing.
              - '.github/actions/**'
              - 'Cargo.lock'
      - if: steps.filter.outputs.sessions == 'false'
        run: echo "No session-related changes; nothing to run."
      # dtolnay/rust-toolchain: SHA-pinned to master; the `toolchain:` input
      # below is mandatory, not stylistic -- see CLAUDE.md.
      - if: steps.filter.outputs.sessions == 'true'
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@683b588c487a69d01f6c6ddf40f036ff682cc2c8
        with:
          toolchain: stable

1	# Crate overview
2	
3	The workspace is **21 crates** under `crates/`, all named `paigasus-helikon-*` (plus the `paigasus-helikon` facade itself), plus three further internal, non-published Cargo workspace members outside `crates/` (see below). This page is the ownership map: one row per crate, what it owns, whether it is published, and how the crates depend on each other.
4	
5	For orientation — how to pick crates and add them to your `Cargo.toml` — see [workspace layout](../getting-started/workspace-layout.md). For the rendered rustdoc, see [API docs](./api-docs.md).
6	
7	## Dependency direction
8	
9	- `paigasus-helikon-core` is the root: it owns the trait surface, the agent loop, the event stream, and the carrier types. It depends on no other workspace crate.
10	- The provider, session, tool, MCP, and runtime crates each depend on `core` and on nothing else in the workspace (`-tools` carries a path-only dev-dep on `-providers-openai` for an example; it is stripped from the published manifest).
11	- `paigasus-helikon-macros` is a proc-macro crate; its `#[tool]` expansion targets `core` types in the consumer's crate.
12	- `paigasus-helikon` is the **facade**: it re-exports `core` unconditionally and the sibling crates behind Cargo features. Application crates normally depend on the facade alone and turn on the features they need.

1	# SMA-826 — Move the shared core test helpers into `tests/common`
2	
3	Size: a small change. Test-only. No public API, book or README change.
4	
5	## Intent
6	
7	Three core integration test files keep their own copies of the same test
8	helpers. A change to one copy does not reach the other copies, and no test
9	fails when they drift. SMA-810 changed the pairing oracle and had to change
10	each copy by hand. After this change, each helper has one source in core.
11	
12	One copy of the oracle stays in runtime-tokio. No test catches drift between
13	that copy and the core source. We accept this because a shared crate is out
14	of scope. Doc comments in both directions name the other copy.
15	
16	## Current state (measured on `main` at `e7ac5377`)
17	
18	| Helper | Copies | Difference between copies |
19	|---|---|---|
20	| `assert_tool_calls_paired` | `tests/deferred_resume.rs:579`, `tests/handoff_transfer_result.rs:187`; runtime-tokio `tests/deferred.rs:427` | The code is equal in all three. Only comments differ. The `handoff_transfer_result.rs` doc comment has one more sentence about the round rule. The `deferred_resume.rs` and runtime-tokio copies have inline comments. |
21	| `DeferB` | `tests/deferred_resume.rs:24`, `tests/handoff_transfer_result.rs:601`, `tests/subagent_propagation.rs:338` | The `subagent_propagation.rs` copy uses the prompt `"policy says wait"`; the other two use `"pay?"`. |
22	| `RequestLog` | `tests/deferred_resume.rs:45`, `tests/handoff_transfer_result.rs:622` | None. |
23	| `CapturingModel` (not named in the issue) | `tests/subagent_propagation.rs:359` | Same behaviour as `RequestLog`. It has no constructor and no `requests()` getter; the test reads the field directly. |
24	
25	`tests/common/mod.rs` already exists. 25 core test files include it with
26	`#[path = "common/mod.rs"] mod common;`. It has `#![allow(dead_code, ...)]`, so
27	a helper that one binary does not use causes no warning.
28	
29	## Goals
30	
31	- `assert_tool_calls_paired`, `DeferB` and `RequestLog` are `pub` items in
32	  `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/tests/common/mod.rs`. The three test files
33	  import them from `common` and keep no local copy.
34	- `CapturingModel` in `subagent_propagation.rs` is removed. Its test uses
35	  `RequestLog`.
36	- Each test keeps its behaviour. `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-core` passes,
37	  and the test count of each changed test binary does not change.
38	- The runtime-tokio copy of `assert_tool_calls_paired` gets a doc comment that
39	  names `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/tests/common/mod.rs` as the source.
40	
41	## Non-goals
42	
43	- No shared crate between core and runtime-tokio (the issue excludes it).
44	- No change to the runtime-tokio permission policies `DeferPolicy`
45	  (`tests/deferred.rs:31`) and `DeferPay` (`tests/turn_checkpoint.rs:317`).
46	  They defer the tool `pay`, so they are not copies of `DeferB`.
47	- No change to the other runtime-tokio helper copies. `RecordingModel`
48	  (`tests/deferred.rs:74-106`) is a copy of `RequestLog` with a different
49	  name, and `with_late_transfer_results` also has a copy there. They cannot
50	  move without a shared crate.
51	- No `exclude = ["tests/"]` in a crate manifest. That changes the published
52	  package contents and needs its own ticket.
53	- No other test helper moves (for example `tool_result_texts`, `call_b_turn`).
54	
55	## Anti-goals
56	
57	- A changed oracle rule. The shared oracle must have the same code as the
58	  current copies, character for character, apart from comments.
59	
60	## Approaches
61	
62	1. **Move into the existing `tests/common/mod.rs` (chosen).** The issue names
63	   this module. All files already include it, and its `dead_code` allow
64	   covers unused helpers.
65	2. **A new submodule, for example `tests/common/deferral.rs`.** A
66	   `pub mod deferral;` line in `mod.rs` would load it, so the 25 include
67	   sites would not change. The issue names `mod.rs`, so this approach is not
68	   used.
69	3. **A shared dev-only crate for core and runtime-tokio.** The issue puts it
70	   out of scope.
71	4. **runtime-tokio includes the core file with a cross-crate `#[path]`.**
72	   The path is outside the runtime-tokio package. Each crate publishes its
73	   `tests/` directory, so the published runtime-tokio tests would not
74	   compile. This approach is not used, and the runtime-tokio copy stays.
75	
76	## Design
77	
78	- **Oracle.** Move it into `common/mod.rs` with the fullest comments: the
79	  `handoff_transfer_result.rs` doc comment (with the round-rule sentence)
80	  and the inline comments of the `deferred_resume.rs` copy. The code does not
81	  change. Add this text to its doc comment: "A copy is in
82	  `crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-tokio/tests/deferred.rs`. Keep the two
83	  copies the same."
84	- **Oracle self-test.** The `#[should_panic]` test
85	  `pairing_oracle_rejects_a_call_after_a_result_while_a_call_waits` stays in
86	  `deferred_resume.rs`. A `#[test]` in `common/mod.rs` would run once in each
87	  of the 25 test binaries.
88	- **`DeferB`.** Move it with the prompt `"pay?"`. *My call:* the
89	  `subagent_propagation.rs` tests check only the prefix
90	  `"permission denied: approval deferred, but this run cannot defer: "` with
91	  `starts_with`, so the prompt text does not change what they check.
92	- **`RequestLog`.** Move it with its `with_scripts` constructor and its
93	  `requests()` getter. Both methods must be `pub fn`, because `common` is a
94	  child module (a private method gives error E0624). The fields stay
95	  private.
96	- **`CapturingModel`.** *My call:* replace it with `RequestLog` in
97	  `subagent_propagation.rs`. It is the same type of copy that the issue wants
98	  to remove. The test then uses `RequestLog::with_scripts(...)` and
99	  `.requests()` in place of the struct literal and the direct field read.
100	- **Imports.** Add `PermissionDecision` and `PermissionPolicy` to
101	  `common/mod.rs` (the others are already there). Remove the imports that
102	  become unused. `cargo test` only warns on them; the clippy `-D warnings`
103	  gate fails. The challenger worked out this list; clippy is the final check:
104	  - `deferred_resume.rs`: remove `Model`, `ModelCapabilities`, `ModelError`.
105	  - `handoff_transfer_result.rs`: remove `Mutex`, `PermissionDecision`,
106	    `PermissionPolicy`.
107	  - `subagent_propagation.rs`: remove `BoxStream`, `CancellationToken`,
108	    `Model`, `ModelCapabilities`, `ModelError`, `ModelRequest`,
109	    `PermissionDecision`, `PermissionPolicy`.
110	- **runtime-tokio.** Replace the doc comment of
111	  `crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-tokio/tests/deferred.rs:427` with the
112	  core doc comment, and change its pointer from `deferred_resume.rs` to
113	  `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/tests/common/mod.rs`. Keep the sentence
114	  "Keep the two copies the same." *My call:* remove "(pre-flight ruling F5)",
115	  because it refers to a SMA-803 working document that is not in the repo
116	  history a reader has. Its code does not change.
117	- **Commit type.** `test(core)` for the core code, `test(runtime-tokio)` for
118	  the commit that changes only runtime-tokio, and `docs(spec)` / `docs(plan)`
119	  for the design files. The PR title is `test(core): SMA-826 move the shared core
120	  test helpers into tests/common`.
121	
122	## Release
123	
124	`test(core)` does not stop a release. Neither crate manifest has `include`
125	or `exclude`, so `tests/` is in each published package. release-plz
126	attributes a bump by file path, and `.versionrc` controls only convco. Core
127	0.5.21 and 0.5.5 shipped from commits that were not `feat` or `fix`.
128	
129	So this PR makes release-plz propose a patch for core and runtime-tokio,
130	and `dependencies_update` cascades to the dependents and the facade. Keep
131	`test(core)`: it is the correct type, and it keeps the change out of the
132	Features section of the changelog. The commit type does not change the bump
133	level here: on these 0.x crates, release-plz bumps a `feat` as a patch too.
134	
135	The SMA-810 core patch (`e7ac5377`) is on `main` and is not released. Release
136	PR #357 carried it, but #357 was closed without a merge at 18:54 UTC on
137	2026-11-20, and no release PR is open. The next push to `main` makes
138	release-plz open a new release PR. If this PR merges before that release PR
139	merges, the test changes go into the same patch as SMA-810. If a release PR
140	merges first, this PR makes a release that holds only test changes. That is
141	harmless but noisy. The merge order is Sven's call.
142	
143	## Verification
144	
145	- Before and after the move, record `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-core
146	  --test deferred_resume --test handoff_transfer_result --test
147	  subagent_propagation -- --list` and compare the test names.
148	- `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-core` and
149	  `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-runtime-tokio --test deferred` pass.
150	- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and the workspace clippy gate pass.
151	- `grep -rnE '^(pub )?(struct (DeferB|RequestLog|CapturingModel)\b|fn assert_tool_calls_paired\b)' crates/paigasus-helikon-core/tests`
152	  gives three lines, all in `common/mod.rs`, and no `CapturingModel`.
153	- Diff the shared oracle against `git show main:crates/paigasus-helikon-core/tests/deferred_resume.rs`
154	  (lines 579-619). Only `pub` and the doc comment may differ. Diff the

# SMA-826 — Move the shared core test helpers into `tests/common`

Size: a small change. Test-only. No public API, book or README change.

## Intent

Three core integration test files keep their own copies of the same test
helpers. A change to one copy does not reach the other copies, and no test
fails when they drift. SMA-810 changed the pairing oracle and had to change
each copy by hand. After this change, each helper has one source in core.

One copy of the oracle stays in runtime-tokio. No test catches drift between
that copy and the core source. We accept this because a shared crate is out
of scope. Doc comments in both directions name the other copy.

## Current state (measured on `main` at `e7ac5377`)

| Helper | Copies | Difference between copies |
|---|---|---|
| `assert_tool_calls_paired` | `tests/deferred_resume.rs:579`, `tests/handoff_transfer_result.rs:187`; runtime-tokio `tests/deferred.rs:427` | The code is equal in all three. Only comments differ. The `handoff_transfer_result.rs` doc comment has one more sentence about the round rule. The `deferred_resume.rs` and runtime-tokio copies have inline comments. |
| `DeferB` | `tests/deferred_resume.rs:24`, `tests/handoff_transfer_result.rs:601`, `tests/subagent_propagation.rs:338` | The `subagent_propagation.rs` copy uses the prompt `"policy says wait"`; the other two use `"pay?"`. |
| `RequestLog` | `tests/deferred_resume.rs:45`, `tests/handoff_transfer_result.rs:622` | None. |
| `CapturingModel` (not named in the issue) | `tests/subagent_propagation.rs:359` | Same behaviour as `RequestLog`. It has no constructor and no `requests()` getter; the test reads the field directly. |

`tests/common/mod.rs` already exists. 25 core test files include it with
`#[path = "common/mod.rs"] mod common;`. It has `#![allow(dead_code, ...)]`, so
a helper that one binary does not use causes no warning.

## Goals

- `assert_tool_calls_paired`, `DeferB` and `RequestLog` are `pub` items in
  `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/tests/common/mod.rs`. The three test files
  import them from `common` and keep no local copy.
- `CapturingModel` in `subagent_propagation.rs` is removed. Its test uses
  `RequestLog`.
- Each test keeps its behaviour. `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-core` passes,
  and the test count of each changed test binary does not change.
- The runtime-tokio copy of `assert_tool_calls_paired` gets a doc comment that
  names `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/tests/common/mod.rs` as the source.

## Non-goals

- No shared crate between core and runtime-tokio (the issue excludes it).
- No change to the runtime-tokio permission policies `DeferPolicy`
  (`tests/deferred.rs:31`) and `DeferPay` (`tests/turn_checkpoint.rs:317`).
  They defer the tool `pay`, so they are not copies of `DeferB`.
- No change to the other runtime-tokio helper copies. `RecordingModel`
  (`tests/deferred.rs:74-106`) is a copy of `RequestLog` with a different
  name, and `with_late_transfer_results` also has a copy there. They cannot
  move without a shared crate.
- No `exclude = ["tests/"]` in a crate manifest. That changes the published
  package contents and needs its own ticket.
- No other test helper moves (for example `tool_result_texts`, `call_b_turn`).

## Anti-goals

- A changed oracle rule. The shared oracle must have the same code as the
  current copies, character for character, apart from comments.

## Approaches

1. **Move into the existing `tests/common/mod.rs` (chosen).** The issue names
   this module. All files already include it, and its `dead_code` allow
   covers unused helpers.
2. **A new submodule, for example `tests/common/deferral.rs`.** A
   `pub mod deferral;` line in `mod.rs` would load it, so the 25 include
   sites would not change. The issue names `mod.rs`, so this approach is not
   used.
3. **A shared dev-only crate for core and runtime-tokio.** The issue puts it
   out of scope.
4. **runtime-tokio includes the core file with a cross-crate `#[path]`.**
   The path is outside the runtime-tokio package. Each crate publishes its
   `tests/` directory, so the published runtime-tokio tests would not
   compile. This approach is not used, and the runtime-tokio copy stays.

## Design

- **Oracle.** Move it into `common/mod.rs` with the fullest comments: the
  `handoff_transfer_result.rs` doc comment (with the round-rule sentence)
  and the inline comments of the `deferred_resume.rs` copy. The code does not
  change. Add this text to its doc comment: "A copy is in
  `crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-tokio/tests/deferred.rs`. Keep the two
  copies the same."
- **Oracle self-test.** The `#[should_panic]` test
  `pairing_oracle_rejects_a_call_after_a_result_while_a_call_waits` stays in
  `deferred_resume.rs`. A `#[test]` in `common/mod.rs` would run once in each
  of the 25 test binaries.
- **`DeferB`.** Move it with the prompt `"pay?"`. *My call:* the
  `subagent_propagation.rs` tests check only the prefix
  `"permission denied: approval deferred, but this run cannot defer: "` with
  `starts_with`, so the prompt text does not change what they check.
- **`RequestLog`.** Move it with its `with_scripts` constructor and its
  `requests()` getter. Both methods must be `pub fn`, because `common` is a
  child module (a private method gives error E0624). The fields stay
  private.
- **`CapturingModel`.** *My call:* replace it with `RequestLog` in
  `subagent_propagation.rs`. It is the same type of copy that the issue wants
  to remove. The test then uses `RequestLog::with_scripts(...)` and
  `.requests()` in place of the struct literal and the direct field read.
- **Imports.** Add `PermissionDecision` and `PermissionPolicy` to
  `common/mod.rs` (the others are already there). Remove the imports that
  become unused. `cargo test` only warns on them; the clippy `-D warnings`
  gate fails. The challenger worked out this list; clippy is the final check:
  - `deferred_resume.rs`: remove `Model`, `ModelCapabilities`, `ModelError`.
  - `handoff_transfer_result.rs`: remove `Mutex`, `PermissionDecision`,
    `PermissionPolicy`.
  - `subagent_propagation.rs`: remove `BoxStream`, `CancellationToken`,
    `Model`, `ModelCapabilities`, `ModelError`, `ModelRequest`,
    `PermissionDecision`, `PermissionPolicy`.
- **runtime-tokio.** Replace the doc comment of
  `crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-tokio/tests/deferred.rs:427` with the
  core doc comment, and change its pointer from `deferred_resume.rs` to
  `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/tests/common/mod.rs`. Keep the sentence
  "Keep the two copies the same." *My call:* remove "(pre-flight ruling F5)",
  because it refers to a SMA-803 working document that is not in the repo
  history a reader has. Its code does not change.
- **Commit type.** `test(core)` for the core code, `test(runtime-tokio)` for
  the commit that changes only runtime-tokio, and `docs(spec)` / `docs(plan)`
  for the design files. The PR title is `test(core): SMA-826 move the shared core
  test helpers into tests/common`.

## Release

`test(core)` does not stop a release. Neither crate manifest has `include`
or `exclude`, so `tests/` is in each published package. release-plz
attributes a bump by file path, and `.versionrc` controls only convco. Core
0.5.21 and 0.5.5 shipped from commits that were not `feat` or `fix`.

So this PR makes release-plz propose a patch for core and runtime-tokio,
and `dependencies_update` cascades to the dependents and the facade. Keep
`test(core)`: it is the correct type, and it keeps the change out of the
Features section of the changelog. The commit type does not change the bump
level here: on these 0.x crates, release-plz bumps a `feat` as a patch too.

The SMA-810 core patch (`e7ac5377`) is on `main` and is not released. Release
PR #357 carried it, but #357 was closed without a merge at 18:54 UTC on
2026-11-20, and no release PR is open. The next push to `main` makes
release-plz open a new release PR. If this PR merges before that release PR
merges, the test changes go into the same patch as SMA-810. If a release PR
merges first, this PR makes a release that holds only test changes. That is
harmless but noisy. The merge order is Sven's call.

## Verification

- Before and after the move, record `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-core
  --test deferred_resume --test handoff_transfer_result --test
  subagent_propagation -- --list` and compare the test names.
- `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-core` and
  `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-runtime-tokio --test deferred` pass.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and the workspace clippy gate pass.
- `grep -rnE '^(pub )?(struct (DeferB|RequestLog|CapturingModel)\b|fn assert_tool_calls_paired\b)' crates/paigasus-helikon-core/tests`
  gives three lines, all in `common/mod.rs`, and no `CapturingModel`.
- Diff the shared oracle against `git show main:crates/paigasus-helikon-core/tests/deferred_resume.rs`
  (lines 579-619). Only `pub` and the doc comment may differ. Diff the
  runtime-tokio function against the shared one. Only the doc comment and
  `pub` may differ.

## Left to the builder

- Where in `common/mod.rs` the helpers go (at the end is fine).
