## Verdict: APPROVE WITH CHANGES
The design is sound. Cargo permits the core → testkit → core dev-dependency cycle for integration tests. The repo has already used this release pattern: published crates with a path-only dev-dependency on a `0.0.0`, `publish = false`, `release = false` testkit, from SMA-330 to SMA-805. The defects are in the verification steps and in some documentation details. No check proves that the moved code stays the same. One check fails every time it runs. Doc text copied as-is breaks the `docs` gate.

## Findings

### BLOCKER
None.

### MAJOR
- **No check proves that the moved helper bodies stay the same** - The spec says "the body is the current body, with no change" (spec lines 75-76, 84-86, 125). Verification (lines 137-151) only compares test-name lists and asks for green tests. A weaker oracle, for example one with a missing `assert!` in `assert_tool_calls_paired`, still passes every test and keeps every test name. The ticket exists because oracle drift went unseen. The SMA-826 spec had this check (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-20-core-shared-test-helpers-design.md:153-156`), and this spec drops it. | Why it matters: "no behaviour change" has no mechanical proof, and green tests cannot detect a weaker oracle. | Suggested fix: Add a step that diffs each moved item against `main`:
  - `assert_tool_calls_paired` against `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/tests/common/mod.rs:429-469` and `crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-tokio/tests/deferred.rs:428-468`.
  - `with_late_transfer_results` against `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/tests/deferred_resume.rs:658-698` and `deferred.rs:1584-1624`.
  - The `RequestLog::invoke` order (push the request, then pop, ignore `cancel`) against `common/mod.rs:407-414` and `deferred.rs:93-100`.

  Only `pub`, the doc comments and the inlined pop may differ. Also require that the test-file diffs hold only deletions, `use` changes and the `RecordingModel` → `RequestLog` rename (`git diff -U0 main -- crates/*/tests | grep '^+'`). As an option, add a one-time mutation check: make the testkit oracle `panic!()` and confirm that tests fail in both core and runtime-tokio. This proves that both crates use the one source.

### MINOR
- **The `git grep` check fails every time, and one of its patterns can never match** - The command at spec line 150 matches the spec itself (line 150). It also matches `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-20-core-shared-test-helpers.md:71,172-173` and `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-20-core-shared-test-helpers-design.md:114`. The text "A copy of the helper in" is split across `deferred.rs:1582-1583`, so it matches nothing even now. Also, `\|` in a basic regex is a GNU extension. | Why it matters: "returns nothing" cannot be met, so the builder either ignores the check or edits historical design files. | Suggested fix: Limit the search to `crates` and `tests` and use `-E`, for example `git grep -nE "Keep the two copies|Copy of .assert_tool_calls_paired|A copy is in .crates/|\(A copy of the" -- crates tests`. Add path checks: `git grep -n "runtime-tokio/tests/deferred.rs" -- crates/paigasus-helikon-core` and `git grep -nE "core/tests/(common/mod|deferred_resume)\.rs" -- crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-tokio`.

- **Doc text copied as-is breaks the required `docs` gate** - The `RequestLog` doc in `common/mod.rs:387` is "A [`MockModel`] that keeps every request it gets." The testkit has no `MockModel`. `cargo doc --workspace` documents the testkit lib, so `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings` fails with `broken_intra_doc_links`. A link to `CANCELLED_TOOL_CALL_TEXT` fails in the same way, because that constant is `pub(crate)` (`crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/session.rs:1029`). | Why it matters: `docs` is a required check. | Suggested fix: Tell the builder to write a new `RequestLog` doc, and to name `CANCELLED_TOOL_CALL_TEXT` in backticks only, with no intra-doc link.

- **The constant `CANCELLED` has two meanings in runtime-tokio** - `deferred.rs:1012` (`cancelled_resume_closes_the_deferral`) checks the text that the current runner writes on a real cancel. `deferred.rs:1617` and `:1692` use the fixed core 0.6.0 legacy text. The spec describes the shared constant only as "the core 0.6.0 cancel text" (line 88). Suppose `CANCELLED_TOOL_CALL_TEXT` changes later. Line 1012 then fails, and the easy fix is to edit the shared constant. The legacy fixture in both crates then writes the new text, and it no longer models real 0.6.0 sessions. Today this coupling exists only in runtime-tokio. The spec extends it to core `deferred_resume.rs`. The same string also appears a third time as `const CANCEL` in `handoff_transfer_result.rs:22` (used at lines 224, 424 and 730, with the live-cancel meaning). The spec does not mention it, although its own reason ("the helper and the assertions must agree") applies to it. | Suggested fix: Either document the constant as "fixed core 0.6.0 text; today it is equal to the live text; do not change it", or keep the live-cancel assertions on a local constant. Decide what happens to `CANCEL` and write the decision in the spec.

- **The dependency list is missing one crate** - A `RequestLog` with its own queue needs `futures_util::stream::iter`, because the current `MockModel` uses it (`common/mod.rs:13,50`). Spec line 67 lists only core, `async-trait`, `futures-core` and `anyhow`. | Suggested fix: Add `futures-util = { workspace = true }`.

- **`Cargo.lock` is not in the wiring list** - A new member adds a `[[package]]` entry to `Cargo.lock`, and the repo commits `Cargo.lock`. The SMA-533 plan staged it by name. | Suggested fix: List `Cargo.lock` under "Workspace wiring".

- **The mdBook edit is not fully specified** - `docs/book/src/reference/crates.md:3` reads "plus three further internal, non-published Cargo workspace members". The spec's phrase "three further members" matches only line 45. Line 10 also lists path-only dev-dependencies as named exceptions (`-tools` → `-providers-openai`), and runtime-tokio now has one too. Line 51 calls every member outside `crates/` a "test harness". The new crate is a helper library that the tests of published crates use, so it is not a harness. | Suggested fix: Name lines 3, 10, 45 and 51 explicitly.

- **The `cargo package` check can be read two ways** - The `.crate` file holds `Cargo.toml.orig`, which keeps the dev-dependency line by design. Only the normalized `Cargo.toml` loses it. `cargo package` also refuses to run on a dirty working tree. | Suggested fix: Write "the normalized `Cargo.toml`, not `Cargo.toml.orig`". Run the check after the commit or with `--allow-dirty`.

- **Close the open "workspace-lints" item (spec lines 163-164)** - I checked it. `tracing_target_syntax.rs:63` and `tracing_target_docs.rs:147` walk `crates` and `tests` looking for tracing macros and `target:` literals, and the testkit has neither. `tracing_target_coverage.rs:49-71` reads only `crates/*/src`. No change is necessary. | Suggested fix: Replace the open item with this result.

- **The Cargo.toml comment must also state the unit-test limit** - Spec lines 106-107 ask for a comment that gives only the publish reason. This repo has no earlier case of a crate X that dev-depends on a crate Y that depends on X. Core and macros only dev-depend on each other (`crates/paigasus-helikon-core/Cargo.toml:34`, `crates/paigasus-helikon-macros/Cargo.toml:26`). | Why it matters: core code in `src/` under `#[cfg(test)]` that uses the testkit gets E0308, "multiple different versions of crate". The next engineer has no local example to learn this from. | Suggested fix: Add to the comment "integration tests only; do not use from `src/` `#[cfg(test)]` code."

- **The oracle self-test sits in another crate** - The test `pairing_oracle_rejects_a_call_after_a_result_while_a_call_waits` (`deferred_resume.rs:520-541`, `should_panic(expected = "starts a new round")`) stays in core. After the move, `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-deferral-testkit` runs zero tests. | Suggested fix: Add a pointer to the self-test in the testkit oracle's doc comment. Put no code blocks in the testkit docs, or set `doctest = false`, so that no new doctest appears.

- **The test-name list does not prove enough** - `--list` also lists `#[ignore]` tests, so a newly ignored test keeps the list the same. | Suggested fix: Also compare the passed and ignored counts on the `test result:` lines. One `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-core -- --list` run covers every binary that includes `common/mod.rs`, which is simpler than naming each binary.

- **The verification run must include `trybuild_ui` on stable** - trybuild adds core's dev-dependencies to its generated project, so the testkit now also compiles under `target/tests/trybuild`. This works by the same mechanism as the macros dev-dependency. But `trybuild_ui` runs only on the ubuntu and macOS stable CI legs (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:155-157`). It also adds a small amount to the SMA-618 cache budget. | Suggested fix: Say that the local run uses stable and does not skip `trybuild_ui`.

- **Commit scopes are not named** - `.versionrc:18` has no testkit scope, so `test(deferral-testkit)` fails the commit-msg hook. | Suggested fix: Name the scopes, for example `test(core)`, `test(runtime-tokio)`, `chore(workspace)` and `docs(docs)`.

- **The non-goals leave other copies open** - Other copies exist across the two crates: `text_turn` and `transfer_turn` (`deferred.rs:248,259` and `deferred_resume.rs:40,548`). | Why it matters: a builder can move them "while there", which adds scope. | Suggested fix: Name them as non-goals.

### QUESTIONS
- I could not read SMA-828, because this session had no Linear tool. Do the Goals (spec lines 14-17) match the ticket's "Done when" exactly? Does the ticket mention `CANCELLED` (the spec calls it "My call") or `text_of`?
- The `text_of` non-goal says "Other tests in those files use them" (line 26). That is not a reason against sharing, because those tests can also import a `pub text_of`. If the real reason is scope, can the spec say so?
- The crate name contains "deferral", but `assert_tool_calls_paired` and `RequestLog` are not specific to deferral, and `with_late_transfer_results` is about the SMA-810 handoff results. Is "deferral" the intended long-term scope? A later rename touches two manifests and `release-plz.toml`.
- Do you want `#[track_caller]` on `assert_tool_calls_paired`? With it, a failure points at the calling test line and not at the testkit. Test names and assertions do not change.

## What's good
- **The cycle and the release model are correct, and the repo has used them before.**
  - (1) Core integration tests and the testkit link the same core rlib. The core lib unit-test build gets the testkit as an unused extern, which is harmless. Core has no features, so `--all-features` cannot make a second core build. `tokio` and `tokio-test` use the same pattern.
  - (2) Cargo removes path-only dev-dependencies from the published manifest. `deny.toml:108-111` (`allow-wildcard-paths = true`) already allows them. `scripts/check-release-gaps.sh:190` skips packages with `publish = []`.
  - (3) The full pattern already went through release-plz from SMA-330 to SMA-805 (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-28-sma-330-production-session-backends-design.md:64,167`). Cite this precedent in "Known limit", because it is stronger than the core↔macros case.
- **The code confirms that behaviour stays the same.** The two `assert_tool_calls_paired` bodies are byte-identical today, and so are the two `with_late_transfer_results` bodies. Both `MockModel`s return `"no more scripted responses"` (core `tests/common/mod.rs:49`, runtime-tokio `tests/common/mod.rs:54`) and ignore `cancel`. Both request loggers push the request before the pop. A standalone `RequestLog` with that order is a correct replacement.
- **The CI jobs that list members or paths need no change.** `scripts/check-doc-coverage.sh:29-30` finds the new crate through `cargo metadata`. `build-no-default-features` builds only three runtime crates (`ci.yml:175-182`). No workflow env changes, so the cache env sync is not affected. `sessions-it` runs because the root `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock` change (`ci.yml:273,281`). That costs time only. The anti-goals and the rejected approaches are clear and have reasons.

## What's good
- **The cycle and the release model are correct, and the repo has used them before.**
  - (1) Core integration tests and the testkit link the same core rlib. The core lib unit-test build gets the testkit as an unused extern, which is harmless. Core has no features, so `--all-features` cannot make a second core build. `tokio` and `tokio-test` use the same pattern.
  - (2) Cargo removes path-only dev-dependencies from the published manifest. `deny.toml:108-111` (`allow-wildcard-paths = true`) already allows them. `scripts/check-release-gaps.sh:190` skips packages with `publish = []`.
  - (3) The full pattern already went through release-plz from SMA-330 to SMA-805 (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-28-sma-330-production-session-backends-design.md:64,167`). Cite this precedent in "Known limit", because it is stronger than the core↔macros case.
- **The code confirms that behaviour stays the same.** The two `assert_tool_calls_paired` bodies are byte-identical today, and so are the two `with_late_transfer_results` bodies. Both `MockModel`s return `"no more scripted responses"` (core `tests/common/mod.rs:49`, runtime-tokio `tests/common/mod.rs:54`) and ignore `cancel`. Both request loggers push the request before the pop. A standalone `RequestLog` with that order is a correct replacement.
- **The CI jobs that list members or paths need no change.** `scripts/check-doc-coverage.sh:29-30` finds the new crate through `cargo metadata`. `build-no-default-features` builds only three runtime crates (`ci.yml:175-182`). No workflow env changes, so the cache env sync is not affected. `sessions-it` runs because the root `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock` change (`ci.yml:273,281`). That costs time only. The anti-goals and the rejected approaches are clear and have reasons.
